Quase lá! Se você dividir cada um dos 5 espaços da segunda reta ao meio, quantos espaços totais você terá? Compare esse novo número de espaços com os 4/10 da primeira reta.

erros.devolutiva: Christian lives 4/10 of a mile from school, so his number line must be divided into 10 equal parts, not 5.
erros.buggyRule: Trocar os denominadores: usar o denominador da segunda fração na primeira e vice-versa.

erros.devolutiva: Start counting at the first interval after 0. Counting the starting mark as 1 can place the point at 3/10 instead of the intended position.
Count the spaces between marks, because the fraction measures intervals. Counting the marks can lead to 5/10.
erros.buggyRule: Contar o número de traços (marcas) incluindo o zero, resultando em n+1 marcas.

erros.devolutiva: The whole line represents 1 mile, so each interval is only a fraction of a mile. The point should not be marked at the whole number 4.
erros.buggyRule: Tratar cada intervalo da reta como uma unidade inteira, ignorando a escala fracionária.

erros.devolutiva: Do not compare only 4 and 2. Compare the positions represented by the complete fractions.
erros.buggyRule: Comparar apenas os numeradores (4 vs 2) e ignorar que 4/10 = 2/5.

erros.valor: Christian lives closer to the school.
erros.devolutiva: Check both marks on the number lines instead of deciding from one numerator. Use the visual positions to support the comparison.

erros.valor: Miranda lives closer to the school.
erros.devolutiva: Do not decide by comparing only the numerators 4 and 2. Compare the complete fraction positions on the number lines.
erros.buggyRule: Comparar apenas os numeradores (4 vs 2) e ignorar que 4/10 = 2/5.

erros.valor: Both live the same distance from the school.
erros.devolutiva: Use the marked positions and the comparison step as mathematical evidence instead of choosing an option because the fractions look related.
erros.buggyRule: Escolher a opção 'mesma distância' apenas porque os números parecem 'simétricos' ou 'relacionados', sem prova matemática.

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?
Use the denominator of Christian's fraction to decide how many equal intervals to create.
Look at the bottom number in 4/... and enter that number in the field.
Set the first number line to have ten equal intervals, then confirm the division.
A fraction on a number line tells how many equal intervals to move from zero.
Start at 0 and count intervals, not the marks themselves.
Move four equal intervals from 0 along the line.
Click the point reached after counting four intervals from 0 on the ten-part line.
What does the denominator represent when a whole distance is divided?
Read the denominator of Miranda's fraction and use it as the number of equal intervals.
Look at the bottom number in 2/5 before entering your answer.
Set Miranda's line to five equal intervals and confirm the division.
The numerator tells how many equal intervals to count from zero.
Begin at 0 and count the intervals on Miranda's five-part number line.
Move two intervals from 0, using the five equal parts as your scale.
Click the point reached after two intervals on the five-part line.
Compare the positions of the two marks from the same starting point, 0.
Place the two fraction representations on the same scale and inspect their relative positions.
Focus on the marked locations rather than comparing the numerators alone.
Use the comparison display to select the fraction associated with the closer-school choice.
Use the marked positions on the number lines as evidence for your choice.
Compare each distance with 0 and choose the statement that matches the closer marked location.
Select the option naming the student whose distance is represented by 4/10.
In the selector, choose the statement beginning with the name Christian.
Review whether both number lines and the comparison choice are complete.
Check the two divisions, the two marked points, and the selected comparison before submitting.
Make sure no required field on the fixed tutor screen is still waiting for confirmation.
When every required action is complete, press the Done button once.

exercicio.statement:
Christian and Miranda both go to Carmite Middle School. They measured the distance between their home and the school to figure out who lives closer to the school. Use the number line to find out.
Christian lives 4/10 of a mile from the school.
Miranda lives 2/5 of a mile from the school.
Who lives closer to school?
